phase: phase 5 (2026-10-26) — visual details: element decision records
provenance: Written in this branch, in this branch's words, from the piece's evidence: the settled transcript (phase 3), the verified compartment inventory (phase 4), and the first draft's in-scene decision records (its #decisions block) as evidence. The record IDS are the piece's decision vocabulary and are kept; the texts are this branch's decisions, each stating what would change it.

records.choice: The settled transcript of phase 3, verbatim. The consolidation weighed a genuinely different candidate and adopted this text as a conclusion; the scene and the voice serve this text and no other.
records.alternatives: Any wording change — a transcript change is a new consolidation (phase 3 reopens), never an edit smuggled into the scene or the audio.
records.context: Consolidation record: transcript/consolidation.md; editor pass: transcript/delivery.md.
records.why: One variable at a time, in developmental order: words settle before pictures and sound are judged against them.
records.change: A canon ruling or a retention signal against a line — via a reopened consolidation.

records.choice: The branch's programme audio is the CLONE-VERIFIED narration (phase 6, audio/audio.json): Hadi's cloned voice fitted at the settled line starts over the piece's music bed, bed a constant −2.22 dB under narration; the bed plays continuously — pauses are narration events, never bed cuts. The scene's embedded audio is a preview copy only.
records.alternatives: Re-mixing or re-mastering the bed — rejected: the bed and its balance were never a defect, and the fit standard forbids re-rolling verified takes.
records.why: The voice is the owner's; the standard exists so its fit is a construction, not a hope.
records.change: A failed line under the fit standard's stop rule — handled in audio/, never by ear alone.

records.choice: Words pop into the planned empty lower band (centres y=1290/1410, alternating), centred at x=530, DejaVu Sans Bold 62 px, chalk; key words amber (the ACCENTS sets) with an overshoot pop. No plate, no band, no subtitle line anywhere in the DOM.
records.alternatives: The caption plate (BANNED, V-16) and the fast-lane caption drawer (the historic overflow source).
records.context: QC V-16 + V-14 safe rect (x[100,960], y[250,1500]); the word-animation discipline: words live in the picture's negative space, timed to speech.
records.why: The lower third is empty in every compartment of this piece by design — the words belong there, inside the picture, not under it.
records.change: If a future compartment's art fills the lower band, the bands move per-compartment by a new record, as in the Ep.2 scene pattern.

records.choice: Phrases of at most 3 words; every phrase group's rendered width is asserted at build time (PIL measurement of the embedded font) at ≤840 px, and re-asserted on live DOM rects and rendered-frame pixel scans at QC. A failed assert stops the build.
records.alternatives: Trusting the drawer — the first draft's i1/i2 failure mode (letters clipped by the frame edge itself).
records.context: Final-QC defect D-1 class: a recurring defect indicts the workflow, so the guarantee lives in the build, not in one piece's numbers.
records.why: Legibility is guaranteed by construction or it is not guaranteed at all.
records.change: Nothing relaxes this; a wider group needs a smaller font, never a wider rect.

records.choice: Word timings from forced alignment on the voice track; words arrive cumulatively inside a phrase at their spoken moments, and a completed phrase HOLDS while the next phrase reveals, clearing when the phrase after next starts (C-05). At most two phrases (≤6 words) exist at any instant, in the two alternating bands.
records.alternatives: Whole-line captions (banned) and per-word karaoke over a standing line (a standing line is a subtitle).
records.context: QC C-05 dwell floor (measured sweep, 2026-10-25: the older clear-at-next-phrase rule left a 0.20–0.51 s median dwell against the 0.83 s floor — the hold rule is the measured fix). One accepted exception rides with this record (below).
records.why: Every word still arrives exactly with its spoken moment — only the completed phrase's clear moves. Reading speed is respected without freezing the picture.
records.change: Alignment boundary error >~150 ms on a re-alignment of the voice track.

records.choice: The flagship container (academy intro, subscribe outro, series header) is built as HTML components inside the scene on the same timeline — the MP4 renders from this file alone (H-01), so the container lives in the scene, not in a post-wrap. All header furniture sits inside the safe rect.
records.alternatives: Keeping an ffmpeg concat wrap (fails H-01 single-source) or dropping the container (changes content).
records.context: H-01; the stricter safe-rect reading is taken even where the older container furniture was once exempted.
records.why: One file is the whole video, container included — that is what makes the file system the video.
records.change: A container redesign applies series-wide, not inside one piece.

records.choice: '1.2 Billion People Use AI Every Week. Almost None Own It.' — the title states the fact and the gap in the message's own terms.
records.alternatives: A question-form title — rejected: the piece is a report; its title carries the finding, and the question lives inside the piece (phase 2) where it can be answered.
records.context: Title/cover discipline S-09; the title predates the rebuild and survives it because it already does the decided message's work.
records.why: A cold viewer should get the piece's whole argument from the title and owe the video only the proof.

records.choice: The L4 turn frame — the crowd greyed, a handful of dots still lit — stands as the cover.
records.alternatives: The L2 number frame — rejected: the number is the hook inside the piece; the cover's job is the distinction (owners lit inside a grey crowd), which is the piece's own visual thesis.
records.context: S-09; the l4-crowd compartment is the piece's signature image (its frame also served the first draft's upload package).
records.why: The cover should promise the turn, not repeat the hook.

records.choice: Role: APPLY (metadata fields.role). Objective: the phase-1 objective, verbatim. Payoff schedule: number (L2) → habit (L3) → turn (L4) → mechanism (L5) → payoff (L6) → bridge spends the conviction.
records.alternatives: INTRODUCE — rejected: teaching the doctrine from zero is the Toaster song's and Lesson 1's job; this lane reports and applies.
records.context: Phase 1–2 records of this branch; the first draft's STRUCT-2 re-audit reached the same role after finding it unrecorded — the drift risk it named is why this record exists.
records.why: An unrecorded role drifts: the next SoA piece inherits the stance only if it is written down.
records.change: A lane-level ruling that SoA pieces teach rather than report.

records.element: End referral — bridge card after the punchline (H6)
records.choice: The bridge compartment decided in metadata fields.end_referral: silent card, 28.833→30.848 s, bed only — NEXT → 'Renters can become owners.' → toaster symbol → 'WHO OWNS THE TOASTER?' → 'the song that asks who owns the layer' → 'tap to watch →'. The long-form's title is never dropped bare: the same card says what it is (a song) and what it asks (who owns the layer). Target: 'Who Owns the Toaster?' (fg2cV8sh3kY), the funnel long-form.
records.alternatives: (a) A spoken referral line — rejected: it would talk over the aphorism's close. (b) Description/pinned-comment link only — rejected: it routes nobody from inside the piece. (c) Referral inside the L6 frame — rejected: the close must land clean before the route is offered.
records.context: The funnel ruling (Toaster + Doorway are the funnel; shorts are judged by onward movement into them); navigation budget: 5.9% of the piece, inside the ≤10% cap (pause map, delivery.md).
records.why: The objective ends at ownership; a viewer the punchline convinces is owed the route to the ownership teaching at the exact moment of conviction.
records.change: Funnel evidence (onward movement from this piece) at the 48 h scoreboard.

records.element: Audio — +2.000 s bed extension at the outro boundary
records.choice: The programme is extended by exactly 2.000 s of the piece's own bed, spliced at the outro boundary (28.848 s) from the wrapped music-only programme (correlation 0.9957 with the main bed in the overlap window), 5 ms edge micro-fades at the joins; narration, mix and mastering untouched; the single AAC encode still happens once, at render (A-09). Total 32.348 → 34.348 s. The music-only twin receives the identical splice so the voice-swap pair stays in sync.
records.alternatives: (a) Zero extension — rejected: the tail holds no spare room (narration ends 27.38 s, the payoff holds to 28.833, the outro is a discrete 3.500 s segment — RMS-verified); a bridge would eat the payoff hold or the container close. (b) A longer bridge (3.0 s) — beyond the extension cap this record sets; 2.015 s carries a signpost card, which is all a bridge is.
records.context: DR-BRIDGE (the card needs a readable hold) + DR-AUDIO (the balance it must not disturb).
records.why: The referral is bought with bed, never with spoken words or mastered balance.
records.change: A timing change to the outro segment itself would supersede this splice.

accepted_exceptions.element: Phrase #9 'week, talking to' — completed-phrase hold (rides with DR-WORD-3)
accepted_exceptions.numbers: Hold 0.46 s vs the 0.50 s C-05(a) floor; bound-capped: the following two-word closer 'a model.' spans 0.28 s start-to-start, so the delivered hold already sits at the second successor's start — the form's maximum.
accepted_exceptions.accepted_by: Archer (JOB B29, 2026-10-25); carried into this branch deliberately — the bound is arithmetic, not neglect, and no re-timing of the settled windows removes it without breaking contiguity (phase 3 pause map).
